IS: 9280 -1979 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
WOODEN SHUTTLE BLOCKS FOR 
NON-AUTOMATIC LOOMS 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institu- 
tion on 15 October 1979, after the draft finalized by the Textile Mill 
Accessories ( Other Than Jute ) Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Textile Division Council, 

0,2 This standard is based on the findings of mill tnals of shuttles made 
of indigenous timbers vis-a-vis imported timbeis carried out by Forest 
Research Institute, Dehra Dun in collaboration with ISI and is in line 
with the manufacturing practices followed m the country in this field. 

0.3 The dimensions of the shuttles vary to a great extent with 
the make of loom. This standard recommends sizes of blocks from 
which shuttles suitable for various makes of looms can be manufactured. 

0.4 lot the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS : 2-l%0*. The number ot significant places retained in the rounded 
off value should be the same as that of the specified v alue in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes requirements of wooden blocks used in the 
manufacture of shuttles for non-automatic looms. 

2. TYPES 

2*1 The wooden blocks shall be either of the following types ( set Fig. I ) ; 

Laminated compressed, solid compressed and fibre- coated solid 
compressed.

3. MATERIAL 

3*1 The following indigenous species of timber shall be used for the 
manufacture of solid compressed, fibre-coated solid compressed and 
centre piece of Laminated blocks: 

Hornbeam ( Carpinus spp. ) 
Birch ( Betula spp. ) 
Maple ( Acer spp. ) 
Cornel ([Cornus spp, ) 
Rubberwood ( Hfflea brasihensis ) 
White cedar ( Dysoxyhm malabancum ) 
Khadsu oak ( Qnereus semicorpifolia ) 
Ebony ( Diospyros melanorylon ) 

3.2 Tor laminated sides of the blocks, veneers of any of the species of 
timber included in Appendix A may be used. 

3.3 The Umber used should be well-seasoned (see IS ; 1141-1973* ). 

3.4 The slope of grain shall not be more than 1 in 20. 



♦Code of practice for se^soiwn^ of timber (first rtvtswn ), 



IS: 9280 -1979 

4. FREEDOM FROM DEFECTS 

4.1 Solid wood compressed blocks, shall be free from cracks, splits, 
honeycombing, gum veins, bark pockets and insect damage, 

4.2 Laminated blocks shall be free from checks, splits, blisters, discoloura- 
tion, overlaps, gaps and delaminations. 

4.3 The blocks shall be as far as possible free from pin knots. One or 
two pin knots per block may be permitted provided these do not appear 
in the finished shuttle. 

Note — For description of various types of defects, set IS : 707-1976*. 

5. FINISH 

5 J The blocks shall be unmachined but end-cut and shall be coated with 
wax up to 12 mm minimum at ends. 

6. ATMOSPHERIC CONDITIONS FOR TESTING 

6.1 Unless otherwise specified, the tests For evaluation shall be carried out 
in standard atmosphere at 65 ± 2 percent relative humidity and 27 ± 2°C 
temperature ( see IS : 196-1966|). 

7. REQUIREMENTS 

7-1 The blocks shall conform to following physical requirements when 
tested according to methods prescribed in IS : 1708-1 969J : 

a) Specific gravity 

1) Laminated blocks 

i) Laminated sides 1'05 to 1'20 

ii) Centre piece Not less than 0'95 

2) Solid wood block* I '05 to 1*20 

b) Moisture content and volatile matter 8 to 12 percent. 

7.2 The dimensions of the blocks should preferably be as given in 
Table 1.

a) MctnufacUuei 's name, initials or trade-mark^ if any, and 

b) Name and typo of the block. 

8.1*1 The blocks may also be marked with the ISl Certification Mark.

9, SAMPLING 

9*1 Lot — The quantity of blocks made from the sames species of timbet 
and of (he same dimensions delivered to a buyer against a despatch note 
shall constitute a lot, 

9.2 The confoimity of the lot shall be determined on the basis of the 
tests earned out on Works alerted at random from each lot.

9.4 The number of blocks to be inspected for freedom from defects and 
dimensions shall be according to col 1 and 2 of Table 2. The lot shall be 
considered conforming to the requirements for the above characteristics 
if the number of blocks found defective for any one or more of the 
characteristics are less than or equal to the corresponding number given 
in col 3 of Table 2. 

9,4.1 The number of blocks to be inspected for specific gravity 
moisture content and volatile matter shall be according to col 4 of 
Table 2. The lot shall be considered conforming to the requirements 
of this standard if all the test results for various characteristics satisfy the 
relevant requirements.
